1.2.3.6-f16.text: Ita est. Ps. sceleste. B. dicis vera. Ps. Verbero. B. quippeni. Ps. furcifer. B. factum optime. Ps. sociofraude. B. sunt mea istaec. Ps. parricida. B. perge tu. Ps. sacrilege. B. fateor. Ps. perjure. B. vera dicis. Ps. pernities adolescentum. B. acerrime. Ps. fur. B. babe. Ps. fugitive. B. bombax. Ps. fraus populi. B. Planissime. Ps. impure leno, caenum. B. cantores probos

translations.note: The marked passage leaves out the opening of the sidenote, "Ps. Impudice. B." ('Ps. Shameless! B.'), so it begins in the middle of the exchange. Ps. is Pseudolus and B. is Ballio the pimp, who takes each insult as a compliment. 'Babae' and 'bombax' are mock-admiring interjections with no lexical meaning, so they are kept as written. 'Cantores probos' is an exclamation in the accusative, meaning roughly 'what fine singers!', as if the abuse were music. 'pernities' stands for pernicies and 'sociofraude' for sociofraus. Confidence is medium because some of Ballio's ironic replies, such as 'acerrime', are hard to render exactly.
translations.text: That's so. Ps. Villain! B. You say true. Ps. Whipping-post! B. Why not? Ps. Gallows-bird! B. Very well done. Ps. Cheater of your partners! B. Those are my ways. Ps. Parricide! B. Go on. Ps. Temple-robber! B. I confess it. Ps. Perjurer! B. You say true. Ps. Ruin of young men! B. Most keenly. Ps. Thief! B. Babae! Ps. Runaway! B. Bombax! Ps. Cheat of the people! B. Most plainly. Ps. Filthy pimp, muck! B. Fine singers!

translations.note: Paolo Giovio (Jovius), author of the Elogia, a collection of short lives of famous men.
